scam_example_text: You get an email claiming you won a lottery and must pay a small processing fee to claim your prize.
recommended_action: Do not pay any fee. Verify with the official lottery website or ignore the email.
explanation: Legitimate lotteries do not ask winners to pay fees up front; this is a common advance-fee scam.

scam_example_text: A 'tech support' popup warns of malware and gives a number; caller asks for remote access to fix your PC.
recommended_action: Do not grant remote access. Close the browser and run trusted antivirus software.
explanation: Scammers use fake warnings to get remote access and steal data or money.

scam_example_text: An online seller asks you to pay using a bank transfer instead of the platform's secure checkout.
recommended_action: Use the platform's official payment method; avoid off-platform transfers.
explanation: Off-platform payments remove buyer protection and are often used by fraudulent sellers.

scam_example_text: Someone on a dating app quickly asks to move to messaging apps and requests money for travel or an emergency.
recommended_action: Never send money to someone you haven't met in person. Report and block the user.
explanation: Romance scams build trust then request money under false pretenses.

scam_example_text: A job listing requires payment for training or background checks before you can start work.
recommended_action: Legitimate employers do not charge job seekers. Do not pay; research the company.
explanation: Employment scams extract fees from applicants for fake roles.

scam_example_text: You receive an SMS with a shortened URL claiming your parcel delivery failed and asks you to reschedule.
recommended_action: Check delivery status using the courier's official site or app; do not click shortened links.
explanation: Fake parcel messages lure victims to credential-stealing sites via short links.

scam_example_text: A stranger on social media sends a direct message with a link to a 'free' giveaway that asks for login.
recommended_action: Do not login through links sent in DMs. Verify giveaways on official pages.
explanation: Phishing pages capture credentials by mimicking authentic login screens.

scam_example_text: An app in a third‑party store requests permissions to read SMS and access contacts before installation.
recommended_action: Install apps only from official app stores and review permissions carefully.
explanation: Malicious apps request excessive permissions to intercept messages or harvest contacts.

scam_example_text: You get a message from a 'friend' asking for urgent money via gift cards — but their account was hacked.
recommended_action: Contact the friend via a different channel to confirm; never send gift card codes.
explanation: Compromised accounts are used to request money from contacts using urgency.

scam_example_text: A website offers an investment with guaranteed high returns and pressure to invest quickly.
recommended_action: Be skeptical of guaranteed high returns and consult a licensed financial advisor.
explanation: High-return guarantees and pressure are hallmarks of Ponzi or fraudulent investment schemes.

scam_example_text: A caller claims to be from the tax department and threatens arrest unless you pay immediately via unusual methods.
recommended_action: Hang up and verify with official tax authority contact numbers; do not pay over the phone.
explanation: Tax imposters use fear to force immediate payments; real agencies use formal notices first.

scam_example_text: A rental ad asks for a security deposit via wire transfer before you see the property.
recommended_action: Visit the property in person and verify the landlord; use secure payment methods and contracts.
explanation: Fraudulent landlords collect deposits for properties they don't own or list multiple times.

scam_example_text: You are instructed to scan a public QR code to pay parking but the QR redirects to a fake payment page.
recommended_action: Confirm payment details on official signage or pay using trusted apps; avoid unfamiliar QR codes.
explanation: Scammers replace legitimate QR codes with ones that capture payment credentials.

scam_example_text: You receive an email with an invoice attached for services you never used; it asks for immediate payment.
recommended_action: Verify invoices with your vendor contact before paying; check for mismatched details.
explanation: Fraudsters send fake invoices hoping accounts payable will pay without proper verification.

scam_example_text: A fraudster offers to buy your item at above-market price and asks you to pay 'shipping insurance' first.
recommended_action: Be cautious of buyers offering to overpay; never send money to receive payment.
explanation: Scammers overpay or invent extra charges to trick sellers into sending funds.

scam_example_text: You get an SMS from your mobile operator about SIM upgrade; the caller obtains OTP and transfers your number.
recommended_action: Do not share OTPs and enable carrier protections like PIN; contact operator immediately if suspicious.
explanation: SIM swap attacks transfer control of your number to intercept codes and commit fraud.

scam_example_text: A message promises a government refund and asks you to enter bank details into a linked form.
recommended_action: Access government services only via official portals; do not provide bank details through email links.
explanation: Phishing forms mimic official sites to steal financial information under the pretense of refunds.

scam_example_text: You are instructed to install a 'helper' browser extension that claims to speed up shopping but harvests credentials.
recommended_action: Install extensions only from trusted developers and review permissions and reviews.
explanation: Malicious extensions can read web pages and steal login data or payment information.

scam_example_text: A caller offers a 'refund' for a recent purchase and asks you to install remote-access software to process it.
recommended_action: Do not install remote-access software for refunds; verify with the merchant using official channels.
explanation: Scammers use fake refunds to trick users into granting remote access and stealing data.

scam_example_text: An email impersonates your company CEO asking finance to urgently transfer funds to a new account.
recommended_action: Verify urgent payment requests via a secondary channel and follow internal approval procedures.
explanation: Business Email Compromise (BEC) uses spoofed or compromised accounts to authorize fraudulent transfers.

scam_example_text: You receive a text claiming your package is being held; it asks you to pay a small 'customs fee' at a link to release it.
recommended_action: Do not click the link. Verify tracking on the official courier website or contact the sender directly.
explanation: Scammers mimic courier messages and ask for off-platform payments to steal card details or payments.

scam_example_text: A well-formatted email appears to come from your bank requesting you 'confirm' your login details due to suspicious activity.
recommended_action: Do not reply or follow links. Log in to your bank account via the bank's official site or app to check alerts.
explanation: Phishing emails use urgency and spoofed sender addresses to harvest credentials or trigger account takeover.

scam_example_text: A caller using a cloned phone number pretends to be a bank fraud officer and asks for your OTP to 'secure' your account.
recommended_action: Never share OTPs. Hang up and call the bank using the official number from the bank statement or website.
explanation: Attackers use social engineering to convince victims to reveal one-time codes which allow immediate access.

scam_example_text: An influencer's profile posts a limited-time giveaway that requires following, resharing, and sending a DM with your email.
recommended_action: Check for verification badges, past posts, and official announcements. Avoid sharing personal info in DMs.
explanation: Fake giveaways harvest followers and contact details for later phishing or sale on data markets.

scam_example_text: An app in an unofficial store promises premium features for a one-time 'unlock' via a card payment outside Google/Apple.
recommended_action: Install apps only from official app stores and review app permissions and developer info before installing.
explanation: Malicious apps distribute outside official stores to collect payments and steal personal data or install malware.

scam_example_text: A 'charity' asks for urgent donations after a natural disaster but the donation page URL looks suspicious and lacks HTTPS.
recommended_action: Donate via reputable organizations' official sites or verified fundraising platforms and check registration details.
explanation: After crises, scammers create fake charities to exploit donor goodwill and route funds to criminals.

scam_example_text: You see a job ad that promises high pay for minimal work but asks for a scan of your ID and your bank details for 'background check'.
recommended_action: Legitimate employers rarely demand bank details or scanned IDs before hiring. Verify company contact info and interview process.
explanation: Scammers collect identity documents and bank details for identity theft or fraudulent onboarding of accounts.

scam_example_text: An investment opportunity guarantees 20% monthly returns and pressures you to invest quickly via a crypto wallet address.
recommended_action: Treat guaranteed high returns as red flags. Research regulatory registration and seek independent financial advice.
explanation: Ponzi and pump schemes promise unrealistic returns to lure funds — investors often lose everything when the scheme collapses.

scam_example_text: You receive a message claiming your social media account will be deleted unless you confirm ownership using a provided link.
recommended_action: Do not follow the link. Use the platform's official account recovery feature and enable two-factor authentication.
explanation: Phishing pages mimic platform login screens to steal credentials and take over accounts.

scam_example_text: A contractor sends a changed invoice with a different bank account and asks you to pay immediately to avoid delays.
recommended_action: Confirm invoice changes through a trusted phone number or in-person contact before transferring funds.
explanation: Business Email Compromise or invoice fraud redirects legitimate payments to criminal-controlled accounts.

scam_example_text: A new 'utility' subscription shows a free trial but buries a consent checkbox; after the trial ends, monthly charges appear on your card.
recommended_action: Read terms carefully, monitor statements after trials, and cancel within trial windows using the official method.
explanation: Subscription traps use hidden consent or confusing cancellation processes to charge consumers repeatedly.

scam_example_text: An attacker convinces your mobile provider to port your number to a new SIM and then uses it to reset accounts.
recommended_action: Set up carrier PINs/ passwords, monitor for unexpected service loss, and enable app-based authenticators instead of SMS 2FA.
explanation: SIM swapping gives attackers control of phone numbers allowing bypass of SMS-based authentication.

scam_example_text: A convincing 'CEO' email asks finance to urgently transfer funds to a new supplier account for a confidential deal.
recommended_action: Institute multi-step verification for fund transfers—call the sender using a known number to confirm large payments.
explanation: BEC exploits trust and company hierarchies to trick employees into making fraudulent wire transfers.

scam_example_text: You receive a link to view a voicemail; the page asks for microphone permission and then begins recording audio while mining data.
recommended_action: Deny unexpected permission prompts. Close the tab and run a security scan. Only grant permissions to trusted sites.
explanation: Malicious sites abuse browser permissions to access hardware (mic/camera) or install further malicious scripts.

scam_example_text: A stranger on a freelancer platform requests that all communication and payments move off-platform to 'avoid fees'.
recommended_action: Keep communication and payments on the official platform to preserve dispute resolution and escrow protections.
explanation: Moving off-platform removes dispute protections and allows scammers to disappear after receiving payment.
